desc: Analyze problem: reverse reconstruction converts dynamic insertion into k-th-empty selection.

Write the full solution: parse N and P, build a Fenwick tree initialized with 1 at every position, implement O(log N) k-th-one selection via binary lifting, iterate i = N down to 1 placing result[P_i-th empty] = i and clearing that slot, then print result[1..N].
Test the solution on Sample 1 and Sample 2 by actually running it, confirming outputs "4 2 3 1" and "1 2 3 4 5"; sample tests PASSED.
Verified edge cases (N=1, P_i=1 everywhere) and O(N log N) complexity within constraints.
